clue.text: Prepare to throw custard round church, then clean up the mess

indicators.note: the phrase for readying the pies is placed around the church abbreviation

parts.note: before a slapstick custard-pie fight you would pick up the pies
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A slapstick custard-pie fight in a church, followed by the inevitable mopping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts CE inside PIES, the last word of PICK UP THE PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover order after a disaster is idiomatically to restore things to how they were, the figurative sense of tidying debris.

clue.text: Song of praise captures good time in procession

indicators.note: the song captures the next letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a paean is a song of praise

explanation.surface: A hymn that holds a good moment as it moves along in a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' puts G inside PAEAN to make PAGEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade of floats and costumed people is a spectacle of this kind.

clue.text: Communist body of firm beliefs

indicators.note: the Communist sits in the body of the firm, inside it

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: A Communist group with unshakeable convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body of' puts RED in the middle of CO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word for 'I believe' names a creed, a statement of beliefs.

clue.text: Turn on a brutal Mongol city

indicators.note: turn means change round, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to face down a savage warrior from the steppes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' rearranges ONABRUTAL. ULAN BATOR is the capital of Mongolia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Mongolia's capital, so it is a city of the Mongols.

clue.text: Get a bit of wood

definitions.meaning: get in the informal sense of understand or catch on
a small thin branch from a tree

explanation.surface: Fetch a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to grasp something is to realise it; and a small branch is literally a piece of wood.

clue.text: Lift to reveal embroidery

indicators.note: embroidery means embellishing a story, so the letters are worked over into new order

explanation.surface: Raising a cloth to show off its needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidery' rearranges TOREVEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word for this machine for raising people between floors.

clue.text: Bury in land suffering drought?

indicators.note: a drought means having no rain, so those letters are lost from the land word

parts.note: terrain is land

explanation.surface: Laying someone to rest in parched earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering drought' takes RAIN out of TERRAIN, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a body in a grave is to put it in the ground, a synonym of bury.

clue.text: Party activist around Egyptian statesman, very close to leader

parts.note: ca, circa, means around

indicators.note: the letter goes close to the leader of the name, right after its first letter

parts.note: Gamal Abdel Nasser, president of Egypt

explanation.surface: A political worker hovering near Nasser, very close to the top man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to leader' puts V just after N, the first letter of NASSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes door to door seeking votes is a campaigning worker for a political party.

clue.text: Vest — not vestt!

parts.note: vest is properly spelt with one T, not two, so a single T
vest is properly spelt with one T, not two, so a single T

explanation.surface: Correcting a typo: the garment is spelt vest, not vestt.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke spelling 'vestt' has a double T; the correct word has a lone one.
explanation.definitionFit: This sleeveless undershirt or athletic top is a kind of vest.

clue.text: Popular ingredient of pineapple cordial

indicators.note: the popular word becomes an ingredient, placed within the other word

parts.note: pineapple is slang for a hand grenade, from its segmented shape
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a favourite component of a pineapple drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pineapple' looks like fruit for the cordial but is slang for a hand grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet pomegranate syrup used in drinks, a kind of cordial.

clue.text: Connection suggesting a footballer's been sent off?

parts.words: suggesting a footballer's been sent off
parts.note: a football side with one player dismissed has ten left on the pitch, ten on

parts.words: suggesting a footballer's been sent off
parts.note: a football side with one player dismissed has ten left on the pitch, ten on

explanation.surface: A link that hints a footballer has been given a red card.
explanation.walkthrough: A team is eleven players, so a red card leaves ten on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking joint's projecting piece fits a mortise, making a connection between timbers.

clue.text: A second insect almost knocked over a tiny organism

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so in a down-reading sense the word is reversed
almost means the insect word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: In a split second an insect nearly bowls over a microscopic creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BEE to BE, which 'knocked over' turns to EB.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a single-celled protozoan, an example of a microscopic living thing.

clue.text: Musical dance which is in the middle of Cats?

definitions.text: which is in the middle of Cats?

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Asking which song-and-dance number sits at the centre of the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats looks like the Lloyd Webber musical; the definition means actual cats, whose stomachs hold fur balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball of swallowed fur forms inside a cat's stomach, so it is literally inside felines.

clue.text: Fruit to eat finally scoffed by chairman

indicators.note: to be scoffed by someone is to be eaten, taken inside them

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese leader

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word eat

explanation.surface: A fruit meant to be eaten ends up wolfed by the chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from 'eat'; 'scoffed by' puts it inside MAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically this salad item is a fruit, a berry of the nightshade plant.

clue.text: Having plan to ring say, husband, one acquired hearing aid

indicators.note: the plan goes round the next word as a ring

parts.note: a map is a plan
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone with a plan for a call, and a husband, gets a device to help them hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ring' makes the plan surround the example word; 'acquired' and 'Having' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone that amplifies the voice helps listeners hear, so it is an aid to hearing.

clue.text: Wessex girl returns to tour more rocky county

indicators.note: the reversed name goes around the jumbled word, touring it
returns means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's heroine from his fictional Wessex

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of more are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl from Hardy country goes back to explore a more rugged county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses Hardy's heroine and 'rocky' scrambles 'more' inside her. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England, part of Hardy's Wessex.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an English shire in the south-west, an example of a county.

clue.text: Found his tables to be forged

indicators.note: forged means hammered into new shape, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: Discovering that someone's tables of figures were faked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like a past tense but means set up; 'to be forged' rearranges HISTABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, a synonym in the sense of create.

clue.text: Antipodean city set to fill a river

indicators.note: the set word fills the river, going inside it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
laid means set down

explanation.surface: An Australian town is ready to pour into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' puts the set word inside the river. The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of South Australia, an example of a city down under.

clue.text: Fashion of newsagent's business?

definitions.meaning: the clothing industry is informally called this
a rag is a newspaper, so dealing in papers is jokingly a trade in rags

explanation.surface: Asking whether the clothes industry is really the newsagent's line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for the clothing and fashion industry; the second sense is a pun on rag meaning newspaper.

clue.text: Delivery that is cold turns up in theatre, heading for treatment

indicators.note: the reversed letters go in the theatre word

parts.note: rep is a repertory theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: heading picks the first letter of treatment

explanation.surface: A delivery that turns up cold at a theatre, where it needs treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses IEC to CEI, which goes inside REP; 'heading for' gives T from 'treatment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipt means the act of receiving goods, which happens on their delivery.

clue.text: Go without putting letter, ultimately, in post

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside
putting one thing in another places it inside

parts.note: a stave is a wooden post or staff

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word letter

explanation.surface: Missing out because a letter never quite reached the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R from 'letter'; 'putting … in' sets it inside STAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deprived of food is to go hungry, doing without nourishment.

clue.text: Old chestnut about Frenchman is too much

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: the tree goes about the Frenchman, around him

parts.note: a chestnut is a tree
M is short for Monsieur

explanation.surface: Telling that old chestnut about a Frenchman again is over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnut' looks like a tired joke but is a tree; 'about' puts M inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means excessive or going beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Horse jump awarded top, position, one gathered

parts.note: a cap is a hat awarded to a player picked for the national side

indicators.note: the position word gathers the one inside it

parts.note: a role is a position or post
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A showjumper given first place and a ranking, gathering itself for the leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' puts I inside ROLE to make ROILE.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressage this is a leap in which the horse kicks out its hind legs, a kind of jump.

clue.text: Woman with small house in a state

parts.note: Ida is a woman's name
ho is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A woman with a little cottage in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-western US territory is one of the fifty states.

clue.text: Draw the line in design?

definitions.meaning: to draw the line is to refuse or protest
a design is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An artist asks whether to draw the line in a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise opposition; and an aim or goal is a purpose someone has in view.

clue.text: Be a big hit, on the rise in film

indicators.note: the reversed hit goes in the film title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: in a down clue on the rise means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a six is a cricket hit over the boundary, the biggest scoring shot

explanation.surface: A film where a big hit keeps climbing in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six clears the boundary without bouncing. 'on the rise' turns SIX to XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to have being, a synonym of living or existing in the plain sense.

clue.text: Heels in which leading lady stands up

indicators.note: in a down clue stands up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the leading lady of a show is its star

explanation.surface: High heels in which the lead actress stands tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heels' looks like shoes but means cads.
explanation.definitionFit: Heels and this word are both informal terms for contemptible, untrustworthy men.

clue.text: Some buffalo mistakenly going round Grand Prix circuit

indicators.note: going round means the run of letters is turned to read backwards
some of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A stray buffalo wandering around a motor racing track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ALOMI from 'buffalo mistakenly'; 'going round' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian town's track hosted the San Marino race, an example of a motor-racing venue.

clue.text: It is within girl to change appearance of character

indicators.note: the word is goes within the girl's name

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Something within a girl transforms her personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like personality but means a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting text in slanted type alters how each printed letter looks.

clue.text: Both parliamentary leader and sweetheart represented those in authority

indicators.note: represented in the sense re-presented, set out anew, so the letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of parliamentary

explanation.surface: Both the head of parliament and a lover stood for the establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives P from 'parliamentary'; 'represented' rearranges BOTH, P and SWEETHEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the establishment, the people who hold power.
